case_title: SRI BHAGWAN v. STATE OF U.P.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that the accused poured acid on the victim, causing extensive burn injuries. The victim died one day after the incident. The FIR was initially registered under Section 326 IPC, but the case was later altered to Section 302 IPC after the victim's death. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The High Court affirmed the conviction. The accused was apprehended by witnesses who were present at the scene and who witnessed the act of pouring acid on the victim. The victim's statement, recorded under Section 161 CrPC, was considered a dying declaration and was relied upon by the prosecution. The recovery memo disclosed the recovery of rubber gloves used by the accused during the incident. The victim's statement was recorded shortly after the incident, and he was sent to the hospital for treatment. The medical report indicated that the victim was conscious for at least half an hour after the attack. The accused was not injured during the incident, which was noted as not affecting the prosecution case.
